key_insight: In BiSBr, carrier localization is not intrinsic but is triggered by vacancies that bind hot carriers into defect-bound polarons, diverting them from the band edge.
engineering_relevance: Controlling defect formation during synthesis and post-treatment is critical for preserving mobile carriers and improving performance in perovskite-inspired solar absorbers.
method: Compared intrinsic carrier behavior with vacancy-induced defect effects
Examined both cold carriers and hot carriers via excited-state defect coupling
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that intrinsic BiSBr does not show carrier localization, but vacancy defects create above-gap defect states and pronounced extrinsic self-trapping through defect-bound hot polarons.
watch_item: Results imply that even small vacancy populations can strongly reduce mobility, so defect control and post-processing stability are likely implementation bottlenecks.
paper_title: Carrier Localization in Pnictogen-Based Chalcohalides from Defect-Bound Hot Polarons
